about.title: Personal Injury Help in Oakley, California
about.longDescription: Oakley sits along the busy corridors of Main Street, Laurel Road, E Cypress Road, and Empire Avenue — routes that carry commuters, farm equipment, and delivery traffic through this growing Contra Costa County city of nearly 40,000 residents. Public records show 65 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 79 people hurt and 3 people dead. Many of these reported crashes cluster on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when weekend traffic and errands overlap on local streets. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents — or in a fall, dog bite, or other accident caused by someone else's carelessness — you don't have to sort out the legal side alone. We handle personal injury claims for Oakley residents. We can review the details of what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to reach out, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out early gives you more time to gather evidence and protect your rights under California law.

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Reaching out sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Stop You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your losses beyond medical bills can still be part of the conversation.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and owe no attorney fee unless money is recovered on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Oakley?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a public road defect, the notice period can be as short as six months, so it's worth acting quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Oakley?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Main Street, Laurel Road, E Cypress Road, and Empire Avenue, with reported crashes tending to peak on Saturdays between roughly 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims directly. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial consultation — we'll review your case and explain your options.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for you. Your initial case review is also free.
